mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, increasing discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of >10% in the same month predicts weakening consumer and construction demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month by >10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings power and consumer spending, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates contraction in manufacturing output and reduced corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.6% signals rising inflation, prompting expectations of future monetary tightening and higher discount rates, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1% month-over-month jointly indicate a significant labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 2% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in consumer demand, which is expected to drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other macro conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% signals a broad-based supply-side contraction, which is expected to lower corporate revenues and drag S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both fall by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.
